why: The broker-backed behaviours every SDK must share: does a tool's text arrive, does structured data survive, is an error mapped, is an oversized result refused, does the session name reach the extension, does a variable resolve. Written as CALLS and EXPECTATIONS rather than as code, so four implementations cannot quietly disagree — the failure mode of the previous four hand-written suites.

cases.why: a tool's text result reaches the caller unchanged
structured data survives the trip as data, not stringified into text
a business error keeps its code and message instead of becoming a generic failure
the caller's call id is echoed: a turn subscribes for progress under the id it chose
the agent threads the session name into the extension call
a result over the content cap is REFUSED, not truncated: truncation silently corrupts what the model reads
an unknown tool fails loudly rather than hanging until a timeout
a prompt variable resolves through the extension, not from local config
